articles.title: Studying Cancer Cells in Microgravity
articles.snippet: This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient's risk of metastasis and support more...

articles.snippet: NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface. articles.title: NASA+ Documentary Captures Europa Clipper’s Journey Into Deep Space
articles.snippet: NASA invites the world behind the scenes to witness the story of Europa Clipper’s journey from a far-off vision to a cutting-edge deep space exploration mission with the release of the agency’s newest documentary, “The Europa Concept.” The documentary will air on NASA+, the NASA app, and the agency’s website starting Monday, Nov. 23, and […]
articles.summary: NASA is releasing a new documentary called "The Europa Concept" to show the behind-the-scenes story of the Europa Clipper deep space mission. It will air starting Monday, Nov. 23, on NASA+, the NASA app, and NASA's website.

articles.title: NASA’s Webb Shows How Supernova Dust Chronicles Star Evolution
articles.snippet: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A).  Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a...
articles.summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope captured a colorful image of a famous space cloud called Cassiopeia A. This cloud of gas and dust is left behind after a huge star explodes, and its dust helps show how stars change.

articles.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
